abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] To systematically review and characterize methodological heterogeneity in sepsis case detection using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) and eICU-CRD databases. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed and Web of Science (publication years 2016-2024). Studies were eligible if they applied the SOFA-based Sepsis-3 definition to MIMIC-III or eICU-CRD, provided at least one explicit label-calculation detail, reported a traceable detection rate, and met further criteria detailed in the PRISMA flow diagram. We classified each study by study type and unit of analysis (patients, admissions, or ICU stays) and extracted methodological details on sepsis case detection across 6 domains. For studies with available source code, we additionally examined code structure and repository dependencies to identify methodological decisions across these domains. Of 396 publications screened, 64 met inclusion criteria and 12 provided source code. Sepsis detection rates ranged from 3.4% to 65.2% in MIMIC-III and from 9.8% to 47.9% in eICU-CRD. Substantial variability persisted among studies using identical cohort definitions within both databases (MIMIC-III: 16.9%-42.2%; eICU-CRD: 13.9%-31.4%). In a generalized linear mixed model, between-study heterogeneity was extreme (overall τ²≈0.79; 95% prediction interval for a new study's detection rate 5%-63%), and study-level characteristics-including database, study type, infection detection method, code availability, and unit of analysis-explained only a small proportion of this variance (≈9%), with no characteristic reaching statistical significance. The overall proportion of studies reporting methodological details varied by domain: SOFA calculation (53.1%), infection detection methods (42.2%), temporal windows (37.5%), aggregation methods (26.6%), and missing-data handling (17.2%). Source code analysis identified 321 implementation decisions, revealing heterogeneity in baseline SOFA definitions (SOFA = 0 vs dynamic baseline), temporal windows (infection-centered vs ICU-admission-centered) and infection detection methods (antibiotic-culture matching vs APACHE-based diagnosis). Dependencies among several MIMIC-III repositories suggested propagation of implementation decisions across studies. Clinically validated sepsis definitions yield substantially different detection rates across studies using identical datasets. abstract: [Journal of pain and symptom management] This article describes integration of a large language model (LLM) into the electronic health record (EHR) to identify unstructured goals-of-care (GOC) documentation or discrete data entry. To determine whether a prompt-engineered LLM reliably detects GOC documentation in clinical notes comparable to human experts and can display this evaluation to clinicians in real time. An interdisciplinary team of palliative care experts created an adjudicated reference standard, which was used to evaluate LLM models in detecting GOC documentation. Given this, the best-fit model (GPT-4o) was then integrated with the EHR for a six-month pilot at four hospitals, then released enterprise-wide. GPT-4o achieved the best performance (specificity 0.95, recall 0.74, precision 0.78). Manual audit on AI-flagged notes (n=325) confirmed substantial expert agreement (86%). In subgroup analyses, there was no statistically significant differences across race, sex, or age (specificity range 0.91-1; all p-values > 0.05). At enterprise scale, the model identified 37,000 patients with GOC documentation within approximately two months. In comparison to those without, patients with AI-flagged GOC documentation had higher acuity rates (ICU stay ≥5 days: 30.2% vs 8.2%; in-hospital mortality: 14.9% vs 0.6%; hospice discharge: 10.5% vs 0.4%). Code status changes were also significantly more frequent (29.3% vs 9.9%; p<0.05). Our initiative met the original objectives by providing a financially sustainable EHR optimization that converts unstructured, high-value GOC narratives into real-time discoverable and trackable documentation. Detecting and displaying these conversations is crucial, increasing clinical situational awareness while reducing documentation burden, leading to enhanced goal-concordant care.
zh_abstract: 【Journal of pain and symptom management】本文描述将大语言模型（large language model，LLM）整合到电子健康记录（electronic health record，EHR）中，以识别非结构化的目标照护（goals-of-care，GOC）文档或离散数据录入。旨在确定经过提示工程（prompt-engineered）的LLM能否可靠地检测临床笔记中的GOC文档，性能可与人类专家相比，并能实时向临床医生显示该评估。一个跨学科姑息治疗专家团队创建了裁定参考标准，用于评估LLM模型检测GOC文档的表现。据此，最佳拟合模型（GPT-4o）随后与EHR整合，在四家医院进行为期六个月的试点，然后在全企业范围发布。GPT-4o取得最佳性能（特异度0.95，召回率0.74，精确率0.78）。对AI标记笔记（n=325）的人工审核确认与专家高度一致（86%）。在亚组分析中，种族、性别或年龄之间无统计学显著差异（特异度范围0.91-1；所有p值> 0.05）。在企业规模上，该模型在约两个月内识别出37,000名有GOC文档的患者。与没有AI标记GOC文档的患者相比，有AI标记GOC文档的患者具有更高的重症率（ICU停留≥5天：30.2% vs 8.2%；院内死亡率：14.9% vs 0.6%；临终关怀出院：10.5% vs 0.4%）。复苏状态（code status）变更也显著更频繁（29.3% vs 9.9%；p<0.05）。我们的计划通过提供财务可持续的EHR优化实现了最初目标，该优化将非结构化、高价值的GOC叙述转化为实时可发现和可追踪的文档。检测并显示这些对话至关重要，可提高临床情境意识，同时减少文档负担，从而促进增强的目标一致照护。

abstract: Objective:To characterize the kinds of internal documentation inconsistencies a general-domain large language model (LLM) can surface from real-world discharge summaries, and to identify recurring failure modes that limit reliability at scale. Materials and Methods: We applied a two-stage LLM pipeline---open-ended candidate identification (Gemini 2.5 Pro) followed by context-grounded verification (Gemini 2.5 Flash)---to 3000 MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries drawn as three contiguous 1000-note batches from distinct positions in the corpus. Two clinicians independently reviewed a domain-stratified sample of 268 retained candidates; a third adjudicated disagreements. Results: Stage~1 proposed 11333 candidates; 3461 were retained after Stage~2 verification---machine-generated candidates---with at least one in 69.7% of admissions. abstract: BackgroundResearch data enclaves such as the All of Us Research Program do not allow participant-level data, or models fitted to them, to leave, which makes it hard to deliver case-finding models, which flag patients with possibly uncoded conditions for clinician review, to patients and clinicians. ObjectivesWe describe and technically evaluate a system that fits models outside an enclave from released summary counts and delivers them through standard health information technology interfaces. MethodsWe exported dissemination-compliant summary counts from the All of Us Researcher Workbench and, outside the enclave, fitted versioned models for Long COVID, chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, endometriosis, Lyme disease, lupus, migraine, depression, and anxiety. A model contract (a model file and a written specification), a Python reference implementation, and synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) test patients define the expected outputs. One JavaScript scorer runs in a patient demonstration, a SMART on FHIR clinician application, and a CDS Hooks service. An atlas displays aggregate results. We evaluated the system on synthetic records with automated tests, cross-implementation output comparison, launches through the public SMART sandbox, and a counterexample review of the scoring and display rules. ResultsThe deployed Long COVID model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.67 in a random validation split. The eight self-report models reached 0.61 to 0.82 in identifying self-reporters without a code. The JavaScript scorer reproduced all 162 reference outputs exactly, and all 437 automated tests passed. A counterexample review found 5 classes of failure, including scoring ineligible patients and treating unavailable data as absent, all fixed and added as tests. ConclusionsModels fitted from released summary counts can be delivered through FHIR, SMART on FHIR, and CDS Hooks with reproducible scoring on synthetic records. Real-record interoperability, usability, and prospective clinical performance remain to be evaluated.
zh_abstract: 【背景】诸如 All of Us Research Program 等研究数据飞地（research data enclaves）不允许参与者级数据或基于这些数据拟合的模型离开，这使得难以将病例发现模型（case-finding models，用于标记可能患有未编码疾病的患者以供临床医生审查）交付给患者和临床医生。【目的】我们描述并技术评估一个系统，该系统在飞地之外利用发布的汇总计数拟合模型，并通过标准健康信息技术接口交付这些模型。【方法】我们从 All of Us Researcher Workbench 导出符合传播要求的汇总计数，并在飞地之外为 Long COVID（长期新冠）、慢性疲劳、纤维肌痛、子宫内膜异位症、莱姆病、狼疮、偏头痛、抑郁和焦虑拟合了带版本号的模型。模型契约（一个模型文件和一个书面规范）、一个 Python 参考实现以及合成的 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources（FHIR）测试患者定义了预期输出。一个 JavaScript 评分器运行在患者演示、一个 SMART on FHIR 临床医生应用和一个 CDS Hooks 服务中。一个图集展示汇总结果。我们通过自动化测试、跨实现输出比较、通过公共 SMART 沙盒启动，以及对评分和显示规则的反例审查，在合成记录上评估了该系统。【结果】部署的 Long COVID 模型在随机验证拆分中的受试者工作特征曲线下面积为 0.67。八个自我报告模型在识别无编码的自我报告者方面达到 0.61 至 0.82。JavaScript 评分器精确再现了全部 162 个参考输出，且全部 437 项自动化测试均通过。反例审查发现了 5 类失败，包括对不合格患者进行评分以及将不可用数据视为缺失，这些均已修复并添加为测试。【结论】利用发布的汇总计数拟合的模型可以通过 FHIR、SMART on FHIR 和 CDS Hooks 交付，并在合成记录上实现可复现的评分。真实记录的互操作性、可用性和前瞻性临床性能仍有待评估。

title: Safety, Feasibility, and Acceptability of the MINERVA Voice Conversational Agent for Emergency Department History-Taking
zh_title: MINERVA语音对话智能体用于急诊病史采集试验
summary: Beth Israel Deaconess登记一项250例观察性研究，评估语音AI智能体在急诊采集病史并生成摘要的安全性与可行性。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; conditions: History Taking, Artificial Intelligence (AI); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 250; status: ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION] This study evaluates whether an artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agent called MINERVA (Medical Interface for Navigating the Emergency Room with Voice Assistance) can safely and feasibly gather medical histories from emergency department (ED) patients and produce accurate summaries. The main questions it aims to answer are: Can an AI conversational agent gather and summarize patient histories in the emergency department? Are the resulting summaries accurate? Do they capture essential clinical information? Can an AI agent overseeing these conversations independently identify red-flag symptoms that may need time-sensitive clinical interventions? Adult ED patients interact with MINERVA via either voice chat or typing on a keyboard. MINERVA asks them questions about their symptoms and generates a summary which the patients review for accuracy. MINERVA reviews the conversation for clinical red flags that suggest urgent evaluation is required. Participants fill out a survey providing feedback on their experience. The summary is not saved in the medical record and clinical care is not affected. Physician reviewers will evaluate the safety, accuracy, and clinical value of the MINERVA interview transcripts and summaries using standardized rubrics, including whether MINERVA was correct in identifying red-flag symptoms that may need time-sensitive clinical interventions.

zh_abstract: 【新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center；研究条件：病史采集、人工智能（AI）；类型：OBSERVATIONAL；入组人数：250；状态：ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION】本研究评估名为MINERVA（Medical Interface for Navigating the Emergency Room with Voice Assistance）的人工智能（AI）对话代理能否安全、可行地从急诊科（emergency department，ED）患者处采集病史并生成准确摘要。其旨在回答的主要问题是：AI对话代理能否在急诊科采集并总结患者病史？生成的摘要是否准确？它们是否捕获了必要的临床信息？监督这些对话的AI代理能否独立识别可能需要时间敏感性临床干预的警示症状？成年ED患者通过语音聊天或键盘打字与MINERVA互动。MINERVA向他们询问症状相关问题并生成摘要，患者对摘要的准确性进行审阅。MINERVA审查对话中提示需要紧急评估的临床警示信号。参与者填写调查问卷，提供对其体验的反馈。摘要不会保存在病历中，临床照护不受影响。医师评审员将使用标准化评分量表评估MINERVA访谈记录和摘要的安全性、准确性和临床价值，包括MINERVA是否正确识别了可能需要时间敏感性临床干预的警示症状。
